questions.prompt: Why is `delay until Next_Time;` preferred over `delay 0.01;` for periodic real-time loops?

options.text: `delay until` uses absolute monotonic time (`Ada.Real_Time.Clock`), preventing cumulative drift from execution time and preemption

questions.prompt: What is the Ravenscar profile (`pragma Profile (Ravenscar);`) used for in high-integrity real-time Ada?

options.text: Restricting tasking to a deterministic, analyzable subset (static tasks, single-entry protected objects, no `select` aborts) for WCET and schedulability analysis

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about the `Atomic` and `Volatile` aspects in Ada. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `Volatile` prevents the compiler from caching or eliding memory-mapped reads/writes
`Atomic` guarantees indivisible reads/writes without tearing (and implies `Volatile`)
Both are commonly used for hardware registers and lock-free flags

questions.prompt: What is `Controlled` / `Limited_Controlled` in `Ada.Finalization` used for?

options.text: Deterministic RAII-style resource management via `Initialize`, `Adjust`, and `Finalize` hooks

questions.prompt: Why does Ada's `Storage_Pool` (`System.Pool_Global` vs custom `Root_Storage_Pool`) exist?

options.text: To let developers plug in custom allocation strategies (arenas, fixed-block pools, DMA regions) per access type

questions.prompt: What does `pragma Restrictions (No_Implicit_Heap_Allocations);` or `No_Task_Termination` enforce?

options.text: Compile-time and link-time enforcement that forbidden constructs (like dynamic heap allocation) are never used anywhere in the program

questions.prompt: In Ada 2022, what does `X := @ + 1;` mean?

options.text: `@` is the target name symbol referring to `X` on the left-hand side (`X := X + 1;`)

questions.prompt: What does `select ... or delay 1.0; ... end select;` inside a tasking call do?

options.text: Attempts a timed entry call and executes the `delay` alternative if the server task does not accept within `1.0` seconds

questions.prompt: What does `select ... then abort ... end select;` (asynchronous transfer of control) do?

options.text: Runs the abortable part concurrently with a triggering event (like a timeout or entry call) and aborts it cleanly at abort-deferred boundaries if the trigger fires first

questions.prompt: Why can `use` clauses on many packages in large Ada codebases hurt maintainability, and what are the alternatives?

options.text: `use` clauses obscure where identifiers come from and risk name clashes; prefer `use type`, local `use` inside a subprogram, or package `renames`

questions.prompt: What does `Static_Predicate` on a subtype allow that `Dynamic_Predicate` does not?

options.text: Use in `case` statements and `for` loop ranges because the compiler can evaluate the predicate statically

options.text: `Ada.Real_Time.Clock` is monotonic and meant for intervals/timeouts; `Ada.Calendar.Clock` is wall-clock time subject to NTP/DST jumps
